1. Not on board taken on board on a praecipe as moved on behalf of the petitioner.

2. This petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India is filed praying for the following substantive reliefs:
"(A) That this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to call for the records and proceedings of the case leading to issuance of the impugned allotment letters/notices by Respondent No.1, and upon examining the legality thereof, quash and cancel all such allotment letters, demolition notices or other actions taken by Respondent No.1's officers in respect of structures on the Petitioner's land, which were issued without jurisdiction and authority.

(B) That this Hon'ble Court in exercise of powers under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, 1950 may be pleased to issue an appropriate writ of mandamus or any other writ, order or direction under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, 1950 quashing and setting aside all the impugned actions of the Respondents in relation to the Petitioner's property bearing C.T.S. Nos.364, 364/1 to 74 of Village Oshiwara, Taluka - Andheri, Mumbai, specifically the acts of entering upon the Petitioner's land, issuing notices / allotment letters to occupants,
demolishing or threatening demolition of structures thereon, and/or taking 04/09/2025 P. V. Rane 507.DOC possession of the land for a D.P. Road, without following due process of law and acquisition.

(C) That this Hon'ble Court in exercise of powers under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, 1950 may be pleased to declare that the impugned actions [of entering upon the Petitioner's land, issuing notices / allotment letters to occupants,
demolishing or threatening demolition of structures thereon, and / or taking possession of the land for a D.P. Road] of the Respondents are illegal, null, void and unconstitutional, being in violation of the Petitioner's rights under Article 300-A of the Constitution of India, 1950 and in contravention of the mandatory statutory provisions of the MR&TP Act, 1966 and the Right to Fair Compensation &
Transparency in Land Acquisition Act, 2013, and consequently restrain the Respondents from implementing the 13.4 mtrs.
D.P.Road on the petitioner's said property unless and until the land is acquired by lawful procedure and the Petitioner is paid due compensation in accordance with law.

sentences.text: It is contended that the part of the structures on the adjoining land which is not of the ownership of the petitioner have already been issued notices.
Copies of such notices are annexed at pages 47 and 48 to the petition.

However, the petitioner has not been issued any notice who is stated to be the owner of the land bearing CTS Nos.
364, 364/1 to 74 of Village Oshiwara, Taluka Andheri.
The documents which according to the petitioner would show that the petitioner is the owner of the land, are also annexed to the petition.

It is not in dispute that the land in question has reservation in the development plan namely of 13.40 meters wide D.P.Road and for such purpose,
the land would be required to be acquired by the Municipal Corporation by following due process of law.
The petitioner has not been issued any notice qua the acquisition of the petitioner's land.

The petition is filed on apprehension that there is a threat from the municipal officers to enter the petitioner's land illegally and remove the petitioner from the land without following due process of law.

4. In our opinion, as the petition is filed only on apprehension, we direct the Municipal Corporation that, in the event, any action in regard to the D.P. Road is to be resorted on the petitioner's land, the same would be undertaken by following due process of law.
The Municipal Corporation is accordingly free to issue appropriate notices to the petitioner and thereafter, by following due procedure in law, shall undertake the work of D.P. Road.

5. Needless to observe that the aforesaid order cannot be inferred to mean that the Municipal Corporation shall protect any illegal structure on the landor on any land relevant for the proposed D.P. Road.
The Municipal Corporation shall take action against the illegal structures which are on the road-line and remove such illegal structures after issuing prior notice and following the procedure in law.
The reason being that the illegal structures lack sanctity including those which are on road-line, whether they are on the Municipal Corporation's property or on the private property.

In so far as the present case is concerned, the actions to be taken by the Municipal Corporation against the unauthorised structures in fact would be in compliance of the directions issued by the co-ordinate Bench of this Court in the orders passed on Writ Petition No.2470 of 2024 ( Patel Castle Co-op. Housing Society Ltd. Vs. Municipal Corporation of Gr. Mumbai & Ors.),
7. Keeping open all contentions of the parties, further adjudication of this petition is not called for.
